checks.detail: The exact 25-prime list, 74 composites and 0/1 neither match the independently reviewed certificate. The small-prime divisor lemma and exact per-row checks prove the finite classification.
The proof and on-screen domain explicitly restrict to2≤n≤100. Required divisors satisfy q²≤n inclusively; 49=7² is covered. The display remainder tuple for 97 is (1,1,2,6).
Violet displays answers derived from certified divisibility. The narration and proof do not claim an independent brush predictor or new prime formula.
The note separates instantaneous function-phase values from accumulated rendering history, acknowledges direction/overwrite dependence, and states that four sectors discard within-sector information.
The note does not infer a zero from a color junction or boundary alone. It excludes phase at zeros and warns that poles, aliasing and unresolved features can resemble zero patterns.

For f(z)=z on z(t)=exp(it), 0≤t≤2π, the boundary modulus is exactly 1, a continuous argument is t, and the positive argument change is2π. The entire function has no poles; the argument principle counts one interior zero with multiplicity. Its zero is simple at 0.
The general statement requires meromorphy near the simple piecewise-smooth positively oriented contour and its interior, and no boundary zeros or poles. N and P count multiplicities.
The scene explicitly requires counterclockwise motion; x=cx+r cos(t), y=cy−r sin(t) compensates for downward-positive screen coordinates. It must not reuse the earlier clockwise brush motion.

The model is explicitly f(z)=z, not a new zeta computation. The note retains rigorous enclosures and complete contour coverage, pole accounting, complete zero counts, critical-line membership, and all-height obligations for global RH.
DLMF supports the argument-principle identity and assumptions; Wegert describes phase plots of complex meromorphic functions and established applications. No novelty claim is made.
